manifest.prompt: make a compact, minimal, modern shopping component.
how_to_read: 1. Read the head first: the first 32 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=32, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' shop-component.metadump.json).
2. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' shop-component.metadump.json
3. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' shop-component.metadump.json
4. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' shop-component.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
5. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' shop-component.metadump.json returns whole entries.

essence.one_sentence: A compact, minimal, modern shopping component: by default one product as a quiet card with image, name, price and a visible quick-add control.

poles: the card recedes so the photograph and price carry the eye
the purchase control stays plain, legible and easy to find
tight padding and small internal steps
44 by 44 targets where space allows, with 24 as the floor

readings.reading: product grid with filters and sort

includes: add to cart on a product page

routing.job: always first: the defining tier-1 entries
routing.when: pull first for any job: the most relevant entries (relevance, not rules)

routing.job: understand what compact, minimal and modern ask for
routing.when: before choosing a layout, a palette or a part list

routing.job: build the card markup, its parts and their order
routing.when: before writing any element of the card

routing.job: style the card: color roles, type, spacing, radius and surfaces
specify states, quantity, price, targets, focus and motion
routing.when: before writing the script or the interaction rules

routing.job: check a finished card against the dump
routing.when: after a build, as a self-review

routing.job: write a brief for a subagent that builds the component
routing.when: before handing the build to a subagent

routing.job: explore options: readings, decision points, option groups and exclusions
routing.when: when a choice is open or a reading of the request is in doubt

component-builder.question: Build a compact, minimal, modern product card with a quick-add control in plain HTML, CSS and a small vanilla JS module, using the default reading and the options named in the dump.
component-builder.returns: markup, stylesheet and script, plus a list of decisions with the dump ids each decision cites

ak-hover-only-purchase.term: purchase control shown only on hover
ak-hover-only-purchase.instead: purchase control visible at rest, with the same control also revealed on keyboard focus
ak-hover-only-purchase.text: A purchase control that appears only on hover is hard for touch and keyboard users to reach.

ak-toast-auto-hide.instead: inline notification after the button that stays until dismissed, with focus moved to it when it holds links
ak-toast-auto-hide.text: A fixed toast that disappears after a few seconds is easy to miss, and one with action links behaves like a dialog that auto-hiding would break under WCAG 2.2.1.

ak-label-revert.term: add label that reverts straight back to Add to cart
ak-label-revert.instead: Added to cart label that stays, with a polite status message
ak-label-revert.text: A state label that reverts too fast to notice is a weak signal of success on its own.

ak-icon-only-unnamed.term: icon-only quantity or remove button with no name
ak-icon-only-unnamed.instead: a text name or aria-label that includes the product, such as Increase quantity for [product name]
ak-icon-only-unnamed.text: An icon supplies no accessible name by itself, and identical repeated buttons cannot be told apart by a screen reader user.

ak-shopping-list-app.excluded_sense: a grocery or to-do list app, or the list itself
ak-shopping-list-app.instead: the act of buying from a product card: a shopping component

ak-shopping-trolley-physical.excluded_sense: a physical trolley pushed round a store
ak-shopping-trolley-physical.instead: the cart state of a web shop: a shopping component with add to cart and a line total

ak-compact-car.instead: small footprint and tight, economical spacing in the card

ak-compact-data-format.excluded_sense: a compact data encoding or serialization format
ak-compact-data-format.instead: small footprint and tight, economical spacing in the card

ak-compacted-file.excluded_sense: a file, log or database squeezed by compaction
ak-compacted-file.instead: small footprint and tight, economical spacing in the card

ak-minimal-bare.excluded_sense: bare or unstyled, with no design decisions made
ak-minimal-bare.instead: few elements and a quiet hierarchy, with each remaining decision made on purpose

ak-minimal-mvp.excluded_sense: a stripped-down prototype or minimum viable product
ak-minimal-mvp.instead: a finished component with its full state set: idle, pending, added, out of stock, error

ak-modern-neon.excluded_sense: a neon, glowing or cyberpunk look
ak-modern-neon.instead: current UI practice: neutral surfaces, clear type and one accent

ak-modern-glass.excluded_sense: a glassmorphism look: frosted, translucent panels with blur
ak-modern-glass.instead: current UI practice: solid neutral surfaces separated by space or hairlines

ak-modern-skeuomorphic.excluded_sense: a skeuomorphic look that imitates physical materials such as leather, wood or glossy plastic
ak-modern-skeuomorphic.instead: current UI practice: flat, matte neutral surfaces with clear type

ak-component-electronic.excluded_sense: an electronic part such as a resistor, chip or capacitor
ak-component-electronic.instead: a UI component in a web or app front end: a shopping component

ak-component-ingredient.excluded_sense: a part of a mixture, recipe or chemical blend
ak-component-ingredient.instead: a UI component in a web or app front end: a shopping component

ak-gradient-cta.instead: a solid button in the single accent role, with its label as plain text

ak-glassmorphism.instead: an opaque neutral surface, separated by spacing or a hairline border

ak-neon-accent.instead: one muted accent role, used only for the purchase control and the focus state

ak-drop-shadow-card.instead: a flat surface with a tonal difference from the page, or a 1px hairline border

variants: NEW and SALE and BESTSELLER labels
ak-badge-pile.instead: at most one text status label, and only when the data says so (on sale, low stock)

ak-emoji-rating.instead: a numeric rating with its review count in text, shown only when reviews exist

ak-carousel.instead: one product image, with any alternate views as a plain row of buttons the user activates

ak-exclamation-cta.instead: a plain imperative label such as Add to cart, with state text handled as the behaviour section describes

ak-meant-minimal-bare.excluded_sense: bare or unstyled: default browser controls, no type scale, no spacing rhythm
ak-meant-minimal-bare.instead: quiet hierarchy: few elements, a clear name and price, a deliberate type scale and spacing

ak-meant-shopping-list.excluded_sense: a shopping list or grocery list app; a retail store fixture
ak-meant-shopping-list.instead: online product purchase: one product, its price, and an add to cart control

ck-p-card-parts.text: The card shows an image, a name, a price and one purchase control, in that reading order.

test.spec: DOM order inside the card is image, name, price, purchase control

ck-p-compact.text: The card keeps a small footprint and tight, even internal spacing.

test.spec: card box width and body padding in CSS px, read against the grid cell that holds the card

ck-p-minimal.text: Each element on the card earns its place, and one element leads the hierarchy.

test.spec: number of distinct text roles and decorative marks on one card

ck-p-modern.text: The surfaces and type read as current interface practice, with one accent for the action.

test.spec: neutral surfaces with one hue on the purchase control and focus ring

ck-purchase-without-hover.text: The purchase control stays visible and reachable by keyboard when hover is absent.

test.spec: with hover disabled the control is visible at rest and receives focus from Tab

ck-target-size.text: Purchase and stepper controls reach 24 by 24 CSS pixels, with spacing so neighbouring targets do not overlap.

test.spec: bounding box of each control in CSS px at 1x zoom

ck-text-contrast.text: Name, price and meta text reach 4.5:1 against their background, or 3:1 when large.

test.spec: computed text and background colours, contrast ratio unrounded

ck-focus-ring.text: Keyboard focus shows a ring of at least 2 CSS pixels that differs by 3:1 from the unfocused state.

test.spec: tab to each control and capture the focus ring against the unfocused state

ck-icon-names.text: Each button without visible text carries an accessible name.

test.spec: button elements with no text content have an aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute

ck-status-live.text: After a successful add, a polite status region names the product and the new state.

test.spec: the status region text includes the product name and state, and focus stays on the control unless the message carries links

ck-stepper-keys.text: A quantity control exposes its value and responds to the Up and Down Arrow keys.

test.spec: role spinbutton with aria-valuenow that changes on Up Arrow and Down Arrow

ck-reduced-motion.text: Interaction transitions on card controls drop out under the reduced-motion setting.

test.spec: transition or animation declarations on card controls sit inside a prefers-reduced-motion block

ck-no-gradient-cta.text: The purchase control carries a solid fill in the accent role.

test.spec: no linear-gradient or radial-gradient in the rules for the purchase control

ck-no-glass-or-shadow.text: The card surface is opaque and separated by tone, space or a hairline rather than a shadow or blur.

test.spec: no backdrop-filter and no box-shadow in the card rules

ck-badge-count.text: The card shows at most one text status label.

test.spec: number of status labels on one card

q-reading.text: Which shopping component: product card, mini cart, product grid, order summary, or product buy box?

q-stack.default: framework-agnostic HTML, CSS and a small vanilla JS module; React and Tailwind variants as options

q-motion-values.text: What duration and easing values suit hover and press feedback?
q-motion-values.default: short duration with a standard decelerate curve, values to be confirmed
q-motion-values.resolve: read the Material 3 easing and duration tokens page directly; third-party values conflicted

q-radius-scale.text: What corner radius suits the card, image and buttons?
q-radius-scale.default: small radius on card and buttons
q-radius-scale.resolve: read the Material 3 shape page directly; third-party values conflicted

q-type-scale.text: What numeric type scale and weights suit name, price and meta?
q-type-scale.resolve: no source fetched in this ticket

q-hover-control.text: Is the Add to cart control visible without hover on desktop and on touch?
q-hover-control.default: Assume it appears only on hover or focus over the image.
q-hover-control.impact: where the purchase control reads in the card for a restrained grid
q-hover-control.resolve: inspect the live page in a browser with hover and in a touch emulation

oq-onlyonce-sale-display.term: how a reduced price is shown on Only/Once
oq-onlyonce-sale-display.text: Not established: the homepage sample has no discounted item. Fetch a sale listing or product page to see the sale label and any two-price display.

q-card-image-position.text: Is the image above the text, or beside it in a compact row?
q-card-image-position.default: image above the text, the form the researched tiles share
q-card-image-position.impact: card shape, columns per row, anatomy order

q-stepper-on-card.text: Does quantity sit on the card, or is it chosen in a cart step?
q-stepper-on-card.default: no stepper on the card; an add adds one unit
q-stepper-on-card.impact: whether the inline stepper part exists

request._about: The user's clauses, verbatim. Nothing glossed here.

p-make-component.anchor: make a compact, minimal, modern shopping component
p-make-component.text: Make a compact, minimal, modern shopping component.

vocabulary._about: Candidate vocabulary for the look (Facet A). Words people use for the qualities; not facts. Web search returned style-reference sites and no authoritative lexicon, so these are inferred.

v-calm-quiet.text: Calm and quiet describe a card where the product image and price carry the eye, with few competing marks, low contrast decoration and no urgency devices.

v-honest-airy.text: Honest means the card states price, variant and stock plainly; airy means generous space around the image and text. Together they read as considered rather than decorated.

specifics._about: Numeric norms and standards for the component, from fetched W3C and MDN pages. Values are CSS pixels, contrast ratios and named criteria. Motion durations and corner radii are not recorded here (see open_questions).

sp-target-24.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.5.8 (AA) sets the pointer target minimum at 24 by 24 CSS pixels; smaller targets need spacing so they do not overlap their neighbours.

sp-target-44.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.5.5 (AAA) sets the enhanced pointer target at 44 by 44 CSS pixels, with exceptions for inline targets and essential presentations.

sp-contrast-text.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.3 (AA) sets text contrast at 4.5:1; large text, defined as at least 18 point or 14 point bold, needs 3:1. Ratios are not rounded up.

sp-contrast-nontext.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.11 (AA) sets visual information that identifies controls and their states, such as borders, icons and focus indicators, at 3:1 against adjacent colours.

sp-focus-appearance.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.4.13 (AAA) asks that a focus indicator cover at least the area of a 2 CSS pixel perimeter of the unfocused component, with 3:1 contrast between focused and unfocused states.

sp-motion-233.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.3.3 (AAA) says motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential to the functionality or the information being conveyed.

sp-reduced-motion-css.text: MDN describes the reduce value of prefers-reduced-motion as indicating the user has enabled reduced motion on their device; a CSS media query can test it directly.

sp-spinbutton.text: The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices spinbutton pattern gives a quantity value the role spinbutton, with aria-valuenow for the current value and optional aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax. Up Arrow increases, Down Arrow decreases, and Home sets the minimum when one exists.

sp-status-messages.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 4.1.3 (AA) requires status messages to be programmatically determined through role or properties, so assistive technology can present them without focus moving. Live regions are the usual technique.

sp-name-role.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 4.1.2 (A) requires that the name and role of every user interface component can be programmatically determined, so an icon-only button needs a text name such as an aria-label.

i-touch-choice.text: For a compact card, the add-to-cart control and the stepper buttons can be sized near the 44 by 44 enhanced target, with 24 by 24 as the floor where space is tight, and spaced so their targets do not overlap.
i-touch-choice.never_implies: a 24 pixel control on touch screens is the comfortable size; 24 is the minimum

i-focus-ring-rule.text: A focus ring about 2 CSS pixels wide, in a colour at least 3:1 against both the card surface and the control, keeps keyboard focus visible on a quiet card without needing a shadow or a heavy border.

i-motion-reduced.text: Because interaction motion can be disabled, a hover or press transition can be wrapped so it is removed under prefers-reduced-motion, leaving the state change itself (label, colour) to carry the feedback.

exemplars._about: Illustrative exemplars from the Only/Once homepage (onlyonceshop.com), fetched 2026-11-04. Each says what transfers (a relationship) and what does not (its motifs). Not a style to copy.

ex-allbirds-tile.label: illustrative exemplar: direct-to-consumer footwear grid
ex-allbirds-tile.text: Allbirds' homepage best-seller tiles put the product name first, the price directly beneath it, and two purchase routes on the tile itself: a 'Quick add' link and an 'Add' button. A small 'NEW' label can sit above the name. The fetched page text showed no hover states.
ex-allbirds-tile.transfers: Price set directly under the name, and the purchase action placed on the tile where the shopper is already looking.
ex-allbirds-tile.motifs: The playful product copy, and the two stacked purchase controls, which add choice to a small card.

ex-everlane-grid.label: illustrative exemplar: apparel brand, browsing-first tiles
ex-everlane-grid.text: Everlane's homepage tiles are plain links. Category and collection images carry short labels and a 'SHOP NOW' text link, and no price or add-to-bag control appears on them. Best-seller tile copy reads 'Customer favorites at better prices.'
ex-everlane-grid.transfers: A tile grid can work as navigation only, leaving price and purchase to a product page, which keeps each tile small and quiet.
ex-everlane-grid.motifs: The category-tile layout, the 'SHOP NOW' text link and the value-led copy.

ex-bellroy-highlights.label: illustrative exemplar: leather goods, image-led highlight cards
ex-bellroy-highlights.text: Bellroy's homepage highlight cards pair a thumbnail, a short headline and a link, with a 'New' tag where it applies. The cards show no price and no cart button. The brand voice is plain and warm.
ex-bellroy-highlights.transfers: One short tag per card at most, and a headline that gives the reason to open the card.
ex-bellroy-highlights.motifs: The thumbnail-led carousels, the 'New' tag styling and the brand voice.

ex-card-order-scraped.quote: Add to cart 2Unfold Laptop Bag . Classic $1,328.00 USD
ex-card-order-scraped.text: In the page text each card runs: product image, the Add to cart label, then product name with a tier word ('Classic'), then price in USD with two decimals. Read the name-then-price pair as the visible card body; the image sits above it.
ex-card-order-scraped.never_implies: Does not show that Add to cart is visible on the static card; the screenshot shows no button under any card.

ex-purchase-control-placement.quote: [image] Add to cart Slide Camera Wrist Strap . Classic $198.00 USD
ex-purchase-control-placement.text: Each product exposes one Add to cart control per card, placed in DOM order directly after the image and before the name and price. Visually it is not shown at rest, so it most likely appears on hover or focus over the image.
ex-purchase-control-placement.never_implies: Do not treat the DOM position as the visual position: in the capture no control appears beneath the names.

ex-variant-line.quote: Cash Card Coin Wallet . Classic $338.00 USD
ex-variant-line.text: Some cards carry a small secondary line under the price giving the colour count ('1 color', '3 colors'), and a 'See All' link marks products with variants. Cards without variants show nothing in that slot.

ex-grid-columns-visual.text: Products sit in a three-column grid of equal-width cells on a warm light-grey ground, with wide gutters and generous vertical space between rows. Each cell is a tall image area with the name and price centred beneath it. No badges, sale tags or borders frame the cards.

ex-grid-type-visual.text: Names and prices are set small in a serif face, the name in a slightly heavier weight than the price, both at a size close to body text. The labels stay low-contrast and centred, so the photograph carries the card.
ex-grid-type-visual.never_implies: Do not infer a specific font family from the capture.

ex-grid-tone-visual.text: The whole section stays in neutral, low-saturation tones with little ornament. The copy voice is calm and understated, which the grid matches with its lack of urgency: no countdowns, no sale prices, no added call-out copy beside each product.

ex-capture-limit.text: In the screenshot the product photo areas render as blank grey panels, and a newsletter pop-up covers the hero. The grid's proportions are therefore read from layout, not from the photographs.

ex-onlyonce-price-line.label: illustrative exemplar: vintage design shop, product tile price
ex-onlyonce-price-line.text: On the homepage 'Latest products' row, each tile gives the product name and then the price on the next line. Prices carry a euro sign before the amount with a space between them, and no decimals or thousands separator appear (for example '€ 2490' and '€ 150').
ex-onlyonce-price-line.transfers: Name first, price directly beneath it, one line each: the price is read as a plain fact about the object, with no extra typographic weight.
ex-onlyonce-price-line.motifs: The euro-symbol-first format and the missing thousands separator, which are particular to this shop's currency display.

ex-onlyonce-currency-format.label: illustrative exemplar: euro-priced shop, price string format
ex-onlyonce-currency-format.text: Prices are written as the euro sign, a space, then the whole-number amount, such as '€ 580' and '€ 1900'. The page shows no decimal places and no grouping separator.
ex-onlyonce-currency-format.transfers: One consistent price string pattern across all tiles, so amounts scan at a glance.
ex-onlyonce-currency-format.motifs: The symbol-first spacing and the absence of cents, which fit a shop selling single high-value objects.

ex-onlyonce-no-sale-state.term: Only/Once tile with no sale state
ex-onlyonce-no-sale-state.label: illustrative exemplar: vintage design shop, price with no discount shown
ex-onlyonce-no-sale-state.text: In the captured homepage the four 'Latest products' tiles show one price each. No sale label, badge or strikethrough price appears on any tile, so how this shop shows a reduced price is not established by this page.
ex-onlyonce-no-sale-state.transfers: A tile that carries a single price needs no secondary label, which keeps the price the only number a shopper compares.
ex-onlyonce-no-sale-state.motifs: The absence of any badge; the homepage sample contains no discounted item to show where a sale label would sit.
ex-onlyonce-no-sale-state.never_implies: That the shop never runs sales. Only the homepage sample was seen; the product pages and any sale listing were not fetched.

ex-onlyonce-link-only-collection-tile.label: illustrative exemplar: vintage design shop, category tile with no price or purchase control
ex-onlyonce-link-only-collection-tile.text: The 'Collections' row is link-only: each tile is a photograph with a short underlined name ('Bauhaus Collection', 'Braun Collection') beneath it. No price, no add control and no quantity appear on these tiles.
ex-onlyonce-link-only-collection-tile.transfers: A tile that only navigates can carry a photograph and one underlined name, and leaves price and purchase to the page it opens.
ex-onlyonce-link-only-collection-tile.motifs: The underlined name as the only control, and the photographic collection imagery.

ex-onlyonce-product-tile-no-purchase.term: Only/Once product tile, no purchase control
ex-onlyonce-product-tile-no-purchase.label: illustrative exemplar: vintage design shop, product tile that links without a buy button
aliases: Only/Once product card without add to cart
ex-onlyonce-product-tile-no-purchase.text: Even the 'Latest products' tiles, which show a price, carry no add-to-cart button, quantity field or buy label in the capture. The only interactive element on the row is the category filter ('All', 'Lighting', 'Electronic' and so on) and the 'See all' link. The cart counter sits in the header.
ex-onlyonce-product-tile-no-purchase.transfers: A product tile can state its name and price and still send the shopper onward to a product page, so the purchase decision happens on a page built for it.
ex-onlyonce-product-tile-no-purchase.motifs: The category filter row above the grid and the bare 'See all' link.
ex-onlyonce-product-tile-no-purchase.never_implies: That product pages lack a purchase control; only the homepage tiles were observed.

ex-onlyonce-grid-image-gap.label: illustrative exemplar: vintage design shop, product tiles with tall empty image areas
ex-onlyonce-grid-image-gap.text: In the captured page the product image areas above each 'Latest products' name were blank, leaving tall white space. The capture may have been taken before the images loaded, so the finished tile proportions are not confirmed.
ex-onlyonce-grid-image-gap.transfers: Tiles with generous, square-ish image space let product photography carry the grid.
ex-onlyonce-grid-image-gap.motifs: The large white space itself, which may be a loading artefact rather than a design decision.

patterns._about: From Nic Chan's axe-con 2022 talk on accessible add-to-cart flows (Shopify stores). Entries are the article's claims, interpreted; inferred entries are what they mean for a shopping component.

pt-target-size-24.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.5.8 (Target Size, Minimum) sets a pointer target size of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, with exceptions for targets in spacing, inline text and essential presentation.

pt-focus-indicator.term: keyboard focus indicator area and contrast
pt-focus-indicator.text: WCAG 2.2 Focus Appearance (2.4.13) asks that a visible keyboard focus indicator cover at least a 2 CSS pixel thick perimeter of the unfocused component, with at least 3:1 contrast between the focused and unfocused states.

pt-quickview-symptom.text: Baymard's ecommerce quick-view article says quick views are often a substitute for a poor-performing product list, so an overlay can cover a list that needs fixing underneath.

pt-hover-only-touch.text: A vendor guide (BoostCommerce, a Shopify app, so a weak source for this claim) says a hover-revealed quick-view trigger needs its own place on small screens. Inferred from that and from how hover works: a purchase control that appears only on hover is hard for touch and keyboard users to reach.
pt-hover-only-touch.never_implies: that hover details are wrong in general; hover can add detail as long as the purchase control stays visible or appears on focus

pt-icon-button-label.text: Carbon Design System says every icon-only button needs a tooltip, except for icons with clearly established names or functions, and that its tooltips open on focus as well as on hover.

pt-quantity-stepper-value.term: quantity stepper value exposed as spinbutton
pt-quantity-stepper-value.text: The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices spinbutton pattern exposes the current value through aria-valuenow, and the Up Arrow and Down Arrow keys increase and decrease that value.

pt-quantity-label.term: quantity toggle label, maximum hint and disabled state
pt-quantity-label.text: Singapore's government design system says a quantity toggle needs a label so users know what they count, hint text where a maximum allowed quantity applies, and that a disabled quantity toggle is excluded from form submission.

pt-price-clarity.text: Baymard's product page research treats the product price as one of the most important components, and its discount article warns that ambiguous promotional messaging stops users reading an offer correctly.

pt-sale-price-emphasis.term: sale price and original price emphasis
pt-sale-price-emphasis.text: Google Merchant Center's sale price guidance says the sale price does not have to be the most prominent price on a page, and that when both prices are shown the original price can keep a larger font.

pt-reduced-motion.text: The prefers-reduced-motion media query detects when a user has enabled a device setting to minimize non-essential motion.

pt-add-state-text.text: The article's button pattern swaps the button label on activation (Add to Cart, then Adding, then Added to Cart) so a magnified user sees the state where they are already looking. The author uses it alongside other signals, not as the only one.

pt-live-region-required.term: live region for button state change
pt-live-region-required.text: If the button label is the only state signal, the article calls for a live region. It advises a polite region already present in the DOM whose text is updated, because screen readers handle inner-text changes on a focused button inconsistently. In Q&A the author says a live region on the button itself would conflict, since live regions strip the button's semantics.

pt-wording-revert-vs-added.text: A label that reverts from Adding to Add to Cart happens too fast to notice, so it is weak as the only signal. A terminal Added to Cart label leaves unclear whether pressing it re-adds the item or opens checkout. The article recommends pairing the button label with another pattern.

aliases: after the Add to Cart button
pt-notification-focus.text: After adding, the article moves focus to an inline notification that has tabindex -1, so it is announced without joining the tab order. It places the notification directly after the Add to Cart button to keep users near their context and keep tab stops few.

pt-live-strips-links.text: A notification with action links (Continue Shopping, View Cart) cannot rely on a live region alone: the region reads only the inner text, so the links sound like plain words. The article moves focus to such a notification, and argues against auto-hiding it under WCAG 2.2.1, adding a manual dismiss button instead.

pt-toast-auto-dismiss.text: A toast is a fixed-position element that usually does not receive focus and often disappears after a few seconds. The article says this makes it easy to miss for zoomed users and unusable for interactive content. A toast with a button is effectively a dialog, and an auto-hiding one fails WCAG 2.2.1. It is suitable only for simple confirmations such as Saved.

pt-unique-control-names.text: In a cart dialog with one control per product (multiple Increase Quantity or Remove Product buttons), each control must have a unique accessible name. A screen reader user who hears a list of identical Remove buttons cannot tell which product each one removes.

pt-dialog-labelledby.text: Every dialog needs a label, most simply aria-labelledby pointing at its heading or opening text (for example a 'your cart' heading). The article notes that modal carts commonly skip this.

inf-quick-add-pattern.text: For a shopping component, the article's ranking implies a layered quick-add: the button label changes, a polite live region announces the state, and any confirmation with links sits directly after the button and takes focus. A fixed-position toast without focus is a weak fit when the confirmation has actions. This is an inference from the article, not something it prescribes.
inf-quick-add-pattern.never_implies: A toast with a Close button is a dialog, not a toast.

inf-product-specific-names.text: For a shopping component, give each repeated quantity or remove control a name that includes its product, so every control in a list reads distinctly out of context. Icon-only versions need the same: an icon supplies no name by itself.

decisions._about: Decision points this component will face. Options and tradeoffs are inferred from the researched patterns above; fits_when is a signal, not a rule.

dp-quick-add.text: Options: (a) a visible add-to-cart control on the card; (b) a quick-add overlay opened from a visible control; (c) no add on the card, with purchase on the product page. Tradeoff: (a) keeps the card light and the control reachable; (b) speeds the buy but adds a layer that Baymard calls a workaround for weak lists; (c) is clearest where variants or policies need reading first.
options: quick-add overlay from a visible control

fits_when.visible add on card: one size or one colour, or mostly single-variant products
fits_when.quick-add overlay from a visible control: many variants that the shopper should pick without leaving the list
fits_when.product page only: products with sizing, notes or policies to read first

dp-stepper.text: Options: (a) an inline minus, value and plus stepper on the card; (b) a stepper inside a mini cart drawer; (c) quantity only on the product page. (a) fits when quantity is usually one; (b) fits when a shopper edits several lines at once; (c) fits when quantity changes the variant. Whichever option is chosen, the value needs a name and an announced value (aria-valuenow).

dp-price-emphasis.text: Options: (a) the current price in the strongest type, with the original struck through beside it; (b) the original price larger, so the saving is the message; (c) one price only. (a) fits when the discount is the reason to buy; (b) fits when the saving is the message; (c) fits when the product is the focus and the price is stable.
options: current price strongest, original struck through

fits_when.current price strongest, original struck: the discount is the reason to buy
fits_when.one price only: the product is the focus and the price is stable

dp-motion.term: motion: none, press response or enter transition
dp-motion.text: Options: (a) no motion; (b) a short press response on the purchase control; (c) a short enter transition when the cart or drawer opens. (b) fits touch and press feedback; (c) fits when a panel appears. Under prefers-reduced-motion, (c) can be removed or shortened while (b) can remain as a colour or outline change.

moodboard._about: Moodboard: what the collected images show (visual reading, seen by the builder) and their measured palettes. Seed material for look and composition, not a rule set. Found online; licences not declared by the pages.

media-onlyonce-home.text: Full-page screenshot of the Only Once shop home page (1280 by 5041 px) plus its SVG wordmark. Source: onlyonceshop.com.

media-hardgraft-home.text: Full-page screenshot of the hardgraft home page (1280 by 6045 px). Source: hardgraft.com. Product tiles and a section are blank in the capture because their images had not loaded.

vis-onlyonce-home.text: Long off-white page with large photographs, wide empty gutters and a short centred mission line. Type is light and sans, set large for headings and small for product names and prices. The only colour accent is the red stroke in the wordmark, used once. Collections are three equal tiles; the product rail is a row of four text-only captions (name, price) under photos, with a plain filter row of text links aligned right. What makes it read modern without trendy: few elements per band, no shadows, and generous space between sections.

vis-onlyonce-studio-products.term: single object on pale studio ground
vis-onlyonce-studio-products.text: Product photographs with one object, centred or set off to one side, on a pale grey or white seamless ground with soft, even light and a faint shadow. Objects fill roughly a third to a half of the frame, so the product reads at small sizes (the 375 by 507 tiles). Colour comes from the object itself: black, chrome, orange (egg timer), off-white. No props, no text in the frame. Transfers to a product card: a neutral, uncluttered image box with the product alone.

vis-onlyonce-in-context.text: Two lifestyle shots: a wooden radio on a white sideboard beside a dried-grass vase and a gold line sculpture, and the same radio cropped tight. Warm wood and amber against white walls and grey. Context is a few objects at the frame edge, not a room. Useful as the secondary image in a detail view; busy for a compact card thumbnail.

vis-onlyonce-architecture.text: Black-and-white photographs of a modernist building: a regular window grid, a flat white-grey wall and large sans capitals. Contrast is high, but the image is grey-only and quiet. Shows how a whole-tile, unbordered photo can carry a collection without added decoration.

vis-hardgraft-home-grid.term: product grid with serif name and price
vis-hardgraft-home-grid.text: Three-column grid of product tiles. Each tile is a photo, then a centred serif name, then a price in the same serif, with a small colour count (e.g. '3 colors') under some. Generous space between rows. A centred promotional modal (tan, with a white email field and a full-width button) covers the top of the grid in the capture: a pattern to avoid copying as the default. Typography, not borders or shadows, separates the items.

vis-hardgraft-leather-backdrop.term: object filling a warm seamless ground
vis-hardgraft-leather-backdrop.text: Leather goods photographed on a warm light grey seamless ground with a soft contact shadow. The object fills most of the frame, with a little air at the edges. Light comes from the upper left, so texture reads in the leather. Colour is brown leather against grey: a warm neutral pairing with only small red-and-white accents on tags. Transfers to a card image box: a warm neutral ground that flatters a product without a separate border.

vis-hardgraft-small-goods.term: small goods on a light ground
vis-hardgraft-small-goods.text: Smaller items (wallets, card cases, a camera strap) on the same grey ground with the object smaller in frame, leaving broad empty space. At 74 by 74 px the strap and wallet still read as a single brown or black shape, which matters for a compact card thumbnail. Detail is in the stitching; the open wallet shows cards and cash as contents. Small objects need more ground around them to read as products.

pal-onlyonce-ground.text: Measured pixel samples across the Only Once images: page ground #F9F8F7; product grounds #EFEFEF, #F3F3F3 and #E9EAEC; Braun grey #CCCBCF; near-black #1B1B1B; red accent #EA3A1A on the egg timer, and #EB625C in the wordmark. Sampled from photographs, so values include lighting; not print specifications.

pal-hardgraft-ground.text: Measured pixel samples across the hardgraft images: product ground #DBDAD2 and #DADAD2; page ground #F4F1EB; card white #FFFFFF; warm grey #918983 in the page text. Sampled from photographs, so values include lighting; not print specifications.

anatomy._about: Parts of a compact product card, their order, and which are optional. The default reading is one product card with a quick add; other readings sit in the options group. Layout (which parts exist, in what order) is one layer; visual system, behaviour and accessibility are separate layers.

parts._about: Parts in default reading order. Order follows the researched sites where they agree; where they differ the placement is a decision point (an-purchase-placement).

an-part-image.text: The image is the first part, a tall area above the name and price. It carries the product, so the rest of the card can stay small and quiet.

an-part-name.text: The name sits directly under the image and before the price. Allbirds puts the name first on its tiles, with the price beneath it. A small tag such as NEW can sit above the name where it applies; it is an optional part.

an-part-price.text: The price follows the name on its own line. Baymard treats the product price as one of the most important components of a product page. Onlyonce shows the euro sign, a space and a whole-number amount, such as '€ 580'. How a reduced price is shown is not established by the captured pages.

an-part-purchase.text: The purchase control is a visible button with a text label, so the label itself names the control. Allbirds shows a 'Quick add' link and an 'Add' button on its tiles. Its position relative to name and price is a decision point, see an-purchase-placement.

an-part-variant-line.text: A small line under the price gives the colour count, such as '3 colors', and a 'See All' link can mark products with variants. Cards without variants leave the slot empty.

an-part-state-message.appears_when: after a press on the purchase control
an-part-state-message.text: A confirmation can sit directly after the purchase control. When it carries links such as 'View cart', it can take focus so the links are read as links. A fixed toast that hides itself after a few seconds is a weak fit for a confirmation with actions.

controls._about: Names and states of the controls in the card.

an-icon-name.text: An icon-only control (cart, plus, minus) gets a text name, for example through aria-label, because an icon supplies no name by itself. Carbon adds a tooltip to icon-only buttons and opens it on focus as well as on hover. The tooltip shows the name; it does not replace it.

an-cart-count.text: The cart count sits in a labelled control, for example a name such as 'Cart, 2 items', so the number has meaning out of context. When the count changes after a purchase, a polite live region announces the change and focus stays where it was. In the Nic Chan talk a live region on the button itself can strip the button's semantics, so the region sits beside the button.

an-quick-add-press.text: On press the purchase control can swap its label through Add to Cart, Adding, and Added to Cart, while a polite live region announces the result. A label change alone is easy to miss, and a final 'Added to Cart' label leaves unclear whether a second press re-adds the item or opens checkout, so the label change pairs with a second signal.

an-stepper-anatomy.text: If quantity sits on the card, the stepper reads as a label, a minus button, the value, and a plus button. The value is a spinbutton: it exposes the current value through aria-valuenow, and Up and Down Arrow adjust it. The label says what is counted, and hint text states a maximum where one applies.

decisions._about: Anatomy decisions with options and tradeoffs. Signals are fits, not rules.

an-dp-card-layout.decision: image above the text, or image beside the text in a compact row

options.fits_when: the photograph should carry the product, as in a grid of tall tiles
options.tradeoff: fewer cards per row; taller tiles

options.option: image beside text in a compact row
options.fits_when: the list is long and shoppers scan by name and price
options.tradeoff: smaller photographs; more width for name and price

an-purchase-placement.text: The researched sites disagree on placement. Allbirds shows Quick add and Add on the tile beside the price. Hardgraft's Add to cart comes after the image and before the name and price in page order, and its capture showed no visible button. Options: a control visible at rest on the card, beside or under the price; a control revealed on hover or focus, which Baymard reads as a stand-in for a weak list; or no add on the card, with purchase on the detail page. The choice belongs to the consumer.

options.option: visible at rest on the card
options.fits_when: touch and keyboard shoppers buy from the list
the list is dense and the image is the main action
variants or policies need reading first

shortcuts._about: Tempting layouts that hide the purchase path.

an-fs-hover-only.from: the purchase control appears on hover
an-fs-hover-only.to: a purchase path that touch and keyboard users can reach
an-fs-hover-only.why: hover does not exist on touch screens, and a control that appears on hover is hard to reach by keyboard, so those readers lose the purchase path. Hover can add a visual cue on top of a control that is already present.

invariants._about: Constraints that hold across every card, with the part free to change.

inv-purchase-reachable.invariant: the purchase path is reachable by keyboard and by touch, without hover
inv-purchase-reachable.variable: the control's position in the card, its label text, its visual weight
inv-purchase-reachable.text: Across every card the purchase path stays reachable by keyboard and touch. Its position, label and visual weight can vary.

inv-name-before-price.invariant: the name comes before the price inside the card body
inv-name-before-price.variable: the image's height and crop, the gap between name and price
inv-name-before-price.text: Name and price keep this reading order in every card. The image's size and crop can change.

options._about: options, not requirements: other readings of the request, each a whole component. Each one reuses the card's parts where it fits.

opt-reading-mini-cart.text: A drawer that lists line items with quantity steppers, a subtotal and a checkout button. Fits when the request means the cart rather than a product.

opt-reading-product-grid.term: product grid with filters and sort
opt-reading-product-grid.text: Many product cards in a grid, with filter and sort controls above. Fits when the request means a catalogue; the card here is one part of it.

opt-reading-buy-box.text: A variant picker, price, quantity and add to cart on a product page. Fits when the request means the purchase area of a detail page.

an-layers.text: Anatomy sits at the layout layer: which parts exist and their order. Colour, type and spacing belong to the visual layer; states, input and motion to behaviour; target size, contrast, names and announcements to accessibility. Keeping each property at its own layer lets a styling choice change without changing which parts exist.

an-default-reading.does_not_imply: that a grid, a cart drawer or a product page is ruled out
an-default-reading.text: Default reading: one product as a compact card, with the image on top, then the name, then the price, then a visible purchase control. Quick add adds one unit from the card without opening the product page. The card is a unit a grid can repeat.

visual._about: Visual system for a compact, minimal, modern shopping component: what the three words mean in visual terms, a spacing scale and radius, palette roles with computed contrast, a type ladder, and how surfaces separate. Tokens marked illustrative are starting values; no fetched source fixes them. Sourced numbers (WCAG minimums, exemplar observations) come in through builds_on.

options._about: options, not requirements: alternatives where nothing decides the choice; sample at most one

opt-accent-ink.text: Option: no hue at all. The accent is the ink itself, #1B1B19, and the add button is a dark fill with a white label. Fits when the brand is monochrome and the photographs carry all the colour. Ink on white is 17.25:1.

opt-dark-ground.text: Option: an inverted palette with an ink ground, off-white text and a lighter accent. Fits when the shop's photographs are dark or the surrounding page is dark. The light-ground contrast values do not carry over; recompute them for this palette.

opt-serif-name.text: Option: a serif for names and prices, as the Hardgraft exemplar sets them, with the sans kept for meta. Fits when the shop's voice is editorial. The sizes, weights and contrast of the sans tokens carry over unchanged.

poles: quiet: the card recedes so the photograph and price carry the eye
confident: the purchase control is sized, labelled and placed where the shopper already looks
v-quiet-confident.text: The look is quiet yet confident: the card recedes so the photograph and price carry the eye, while the purchase control stays plain, legible and easy to find. Pushed too far, quiet reads as unfinished and confident reads as loud.

b-compact.text: Compact binds to the card's footprint and its internal rhythm: tight padding and small internal steps. It does not bind to type size or to touch targets, which keep the research 20 floors (24 by 24 CSS px minimum, 44 by 44 comfortable).

modifies: hierarchy between name, price and control
b-minimal.text: Minimal binds to how few elements the card shows and how clear their order is: image, name, price, one purchase control. It means quiet hierarchy, not bare or unstyled output. Each extra mark is asked to earn its place.

b-modern.text: Modern binds to contemporary restraint: a clean sans or a considered serif, a 4 px rhythm, one accent and neutral surfaces. The scraped grid in one exemplar shows this restraint in neutral, low-saturation tones with no badges and no frames around cards.

v-human-words.text: Words people use for this look: calm and quiet for restraint, honest for stating price, variant and stock plainly, airy for generous space, considered for deliberate choices. They describe what the eye sees; they are not a checklist.

p-space-scale.text: A 4 px base unit with steps of 4, 8, 12, 16 and 24 px. Internal card padding sits at 12 px and the gap between a name and its meta at 4 to 8 px. No fetched source fixes these steps; they are a starting token for the builder to adjust.

p-gutter.text: Between cards, 16 to 24 px: at least the internal padding and up to twice it. The Hardgraft grid runs wide gutters and generous vertical space between rows; that is a qualitative read of a scraped page, not a measured value. Open space is what separates cards in this system.

p-radius.text: One radius for the card image, the card and the controls: 8 px at the default, 4 to 12 px across the range. Research 20 left q-radius-scale open (the Material 3 shape page was not read), so this is a builder's starting token. Keep image and card corners on the same radius so they match.

c-surface.text: Card surface, white, on a page ground of #F4F3EF. The two differ by 1.11:1, a tonal step that separates the card without a border or shadow. Ink text reaches 17.25:1 on this surface and muted text 6.69:1 (WCAG relative luminance, computed for this palette).

c-text.text: Name and price text, a warm near-black. 17.25:1 on the surface and 15.54:1 on the page ground, well over the 4.5:1 minimum for text.

c-muted.text: Meta text, secondary price text and out-of-stock labels. 6.69:1 on the surface and 6.02:1 on the page ground, passing the 4.5:1 minimum with room to spare.

c-accent.text: One accent: the add-to-cart fill with white label text at 8.05:1, and the focus ring. A single hue carries the action; the rest of the card stays neutral.

c-state-error.text: Error text, for example a stock or quantity message, at 6.54:1 on the surface. Pair it with words or an icon so colour is not the sole signal; the wording of each state belongs to the behaviour ticket.

p-type-name.text: Name at 15 px, weight 500, line height 1.3, in ink. Research 20 left the type scale unsourced (q-type-scale), so the size is illustrative. The Hardgraft grid sets names close to body size and slightly heavier than price; here name and price share a weight so position and tabular figures carry the price.

p-type-price.text: Price at 15 px, weight 500, with tabular figures so prices in a column align. Weight 600 is an option if the price should lead the card; sale and original price treatment belongs to the behaviour ticket.

p-type-meta.text: Meta (variant count, a short label, a unit) at 12 to 13 px, weight 400, in muted text. Meta stays quiet and stays at or above 12 px, so compact does not turn into tiny text.

surface-separation.term: surface separation without shadows or heavy borders
surface-separation.text: Separate cards by space first (16 to 24 px gaps), then by one tonal step between the surface and the page ground, then by a 1 px hairline in #E4E2DC only where list rows need dividing. A hairline that only divides rows is decorative and can stay faint. A control's own boundary, such as an outlined stepper, uses #8A887F at 3.55:1 on the surface, so it still reaches the 3:1 non-text minimum. No drop shadow is needed.

behaviour._about: States, quantity input, price, target size, focus, contrast and motion for the card's purchase control. Facts cited to researched ids (WCAG 2.2, WAI-ARIA, MDN, Google Merchant Center, captured shop pages). Derived states and choices are inferred; durations are illustrative because motion-duration research is still open (q-motion-values).

states._about: Conditional grammar for the add-to-cart control. Each state names its label and the signals that travel with it, so no single signal carries the state alone.

g-state-idle.text: At rest the purchase control reads Add to cart, is enabled, and announces nothing. The wording matches the label on the captured product card.

then: polite status: Adding [product name] to cart
g-state-pending.text: While the request runs, the label changes to Adding so a magnified or slow user sees the state where they are already looking. The article pairs the label with another signal, so a polite status message carries the same state for screen readers. Duplicate presses during pending can be ignored, which is a choice.

then: polite status: Added [product name] to cart
inline notification directly after the button with Continue shopping and View cart links
focus moves to the notification when it holds links
g-state-added.text: After a successful add the label stays at Added to cart, because a label that reverts to Add to cart is too quick to notice, and a terminal Added to cart label alone does not say whether pressing it re-adds the item or opens checkout. The notification after the button carries the next steps, and focus moves to it so its links are reached without a long walk through the page.

then: visible text reason beside the control
g-state-out-of-stock.text: A sold-out product keeps a visible Out of stock label and a text reason beside the control. The Singapore government quantity pattern notes that a disabled toggle is excluded from form submission, so the state should be readable from text as well as from the disabled attribute.

then: label reverts to Add to cart so retry is available
error text in a polite live region near the control
g-state-error.text: A failed add returns the label to Add to cart so the shopper can retry, and the failure is announced as text in a polite live region placed near the control. WCAG 4.1.3 requires status messages to be determinable by role or property, so the message does not depend on moving focus.

b-stepper-keys.text: The WAI-ARIA spinbutton pattern gives the quantity the role spinbutton. aria-valuenow carries the current value, Up Arrow increases it, Down Arrow decreases it, and Home sets the minimum when one exists. aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax are optional.

b-stepper-bounds.text: The minimum quantity is 1 by default. The maximum is the stock count when it is known, shown as hint text where it applies, for example Up to 5 available. The minus control is disabled at the minimum and the plus control at the maximum, and each disabled control keeps a text name. Name each stepper with its product, such as Quantity for [product name], so repeated steppers in a list read distinctly out of context.
b-stepper-bounds.never_implies: the value 1 is a default; a shop may allow zero or set a bulk minimum

price._about: Price presentation: emphasis, currency and format. Unit price was not found on the captured cards and is unknown here.

b-price-emphasis.text: When a sale price and an original price both show, the sale price does not have to be the most prominent figure: the original can keep the larger font (Google Merchant Center). Baymard treats the product price as one of the most important parts of a product page and warns that ambiguous promotional wording stops users reading an offer correctly. Which figure leads is a decision point, not a rule.

b-price-format.text: The captured shops differ: one prints US dollars with two decimals on each card, and another prints euro amounts as a euro sign, a space and a whole number, such as '€ 2490', with no decimals or grouping separator. The captures do not set the currency for this component, so a neutral single-currency card can use locale-aware number formatting to follow the shop's own format.

targets_focus_contrast._about: Pointer target size, focus indicator and contrast. Researched minimums are the floor; the compact-card choices are inferred.

b-target-min.text: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, AA). Smaller targets need spacing so they do not overlap their neighbours, and the criterion has exceptions for inline and essential cases.

b-target-choice.text: On a compact card, aim for 44 by 44 CSS pixels for the add control and stepper buttons where space allows, and treat 24 by 24 as the floor where it does not. Keep neighbouring targets from overlapping.
b-target-choice.never_implies: 24 pixels is the comfortable touch size; 24 is the floor

b-contrast-text.text: Text reads at 4.5:1 against its background (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3), or 3:1 for large text (18 point, or 14 point bold). Borders, icons and focus indicators that identify a control reach 3:1 against adjacent colours (SC 1.4.11). Ratios are not rounded up.

b-focus-ring.text: A visible focus indicator covers at least a 2 CSS pixel perimeter of the unfocused control and reaches 3:1 contrast between focused and unfocused states (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.13, AAA). A 2 px ring at 3:1 against both the card surface and the control keeps keyboard focus visible on a quiet card, without a shadow or heavy border.

motion._about: Interaction motion. The enforced rule is reduced motion; the durations are starting points.

options._about: options, not requirements: illustrative starting points, not measured values

opt-motion-press.text: Starting point: hover and press colour or outline change over about 120 ms with an ease-out curve. If a transform is used on press, a scale of 0.98 for about 80 ms. Illustrative, because q-motion-values is still open. Under reduced motion keep the colour change and drop the scale.

b-reduced-motion.text: Motion triggered by interaction can be disabled (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3, AAA), and prefers-reduced-motion reports that the user has asked to minimise non-essential motion. Wrap hover and press transitions so that they are removed under reduce, leaving the colour, outline or label change to carry the feedback.

checks._about: Detectable signals a reviewer can run on the rendered card.

sig-purchase-no-hover.text: Check: the add control is a native button with a text name in the markup, is visible at rest, and receives focus from the keyboard with no hover state applied. Detect by tabbing through the card and reading the computed visibility at rest.

lexicon._about: Canonical vocabulary for the look, the prompt's three words and the component. Associations are what the model brings to mind: inferred, tier 3-4, seed material to draw on, not a rule. The wrong senses of the prompt words are in anti_keywords (not_meant), each with the meant sense in instead.

lex-product-first.text: The product's image and name lead the card, and every other mark sits behind them in the order a shopper uses it: image, name, price, then the purchase control. Single-object product pages on a plain field read this way.
lex-product-first.contributes: A reading order for the card: image, name, price, control.

lex-quiet-hierarchy.text: One element leads by size or weight, two or three secondary levels step down, and the remaining text shares one level. Minimal components usually keep the contrast between levels small rather than dramatic.
lex-quiet-hierarchy.contributes: Keeps the type scale to a few steps and avoids competing headings.

lex-less-but-better.text: Dieter Rams's phrase for good product design: remove a part before adding a style. Braun products and Muji's plain range carry the same idea into everyday objects.
lex-less-but-better.contributes: A test for each addition: what does this part do for the shopper?

lex-tight-rhythm.text: A small set of spacing steps repeats through the card, so the footprint stays small and each gap reads as chosen. Compact components tend to use one base unit and its multiples throughout.
lex-tight-rhythm.contributes: A single spacing unit and a few multiples, applied the same way on every card.

lex-hairline.text: A one-pixel rule or an empty gap separates parts of the card. Fill, shadow and heavy borders do that job less often in quiet interfaces.
lex-hairline.contributes: Ways to separate surfaces without shadows or heavy borders.

lex-one-accent.text: Neutrals carry the layout and text, and one hue marks the action, the sale or the selected state. Quiet product interfaces often keep the accent to the purchase control.
lex-one-accent.contributes: Colour roles: neutral surfaces and text, one accent, and state colours kept apart from it.

lex-tabular-price.text: Digits of equal width keep prices aligned when cards sit in a grid, and lining figures sit on the baseline beside the name. Price legibility in a list depends on this more than on size.
lex-tabular-price.contributes: Price typography in grids: equal-width digits and a clear currency mark.

lex-paper-neutral.caveat: an impression from words, not a measured response
lex-paper-neutral.text: Warm off-white and stone greys that feel like uncoated paper, with matte finishes rather than gloss. The family is calm and slightly warm, and it lets product photography keep its own colour.
lex-paper-neutral.contributes: A surface colour family to draw from, as an option among cool greys and pure white.

lex-settled-motion.caveat: an impression from words, not a measured response
lex-settled-motion.text: A short movement that decelerates into place and stops without bounce or overshoot, so the eye lands and rests. The feeling is composed rather than playful.
lex-settled-motion.contributes: A vocabulary for hover and press feedback: short, decelerating, no overshoot.

lex-gallery-label.text: A name and price set like a small printed label beside an object: short, factual, in a fixed order, with room around it. The label informs and does not sell.
lex-gallery-label.contributes: A metaphor for the name and price block: factual copy, fixed order, space around.

lex-low-friction.text: Buying takes the fewest steps, and each step shows what it does. Adjacent to this are the quick add pattern and the inline stepper, both of which trade a detour for a visible control.
lex-low-friction.contributes: A lens for the decision points: the path from card to cart.

lex-editorial-presentation.text: Product photos on plain backgrounds at a consistent crop, with short copy. Aesop, Everlane and Muji use this register to different degrees, and it is one of the reasons their pages read as quiet.
lex-editorial-presentation.contributes: Image treatment: consistent crop, plain ground, text kept short.

lex-current-practice.text: Modern reads as the present-day interface norm: a neutral sans-serif, clear focus styles, modest corner radii and comfortable targets. It tips into trendy when it adopts a passing effect such as heavy gradients.
lex-current-practice.contributes: Defines modern as current practice, which is the opposite of a passing effect.

lex-quiet-brands.text: Names commonly cited for quiet product design: Muji and Braun for restraint, Aesop for considered typography, Everlane and Allbirds for plain shop tiles, Bellroy for warm plain copy, and the Apple Store for product-first space. Their shared traits transfer as relationships, and their visual motifs do not.
lex-quiet-brands.contributes: Named references to look up for transfer. Look at the relationship, not the motif.

exclusion._about: What a model given only the prompt would most likely get wrong: forbidden shortcuts. Each names the shortcut and the instead. Options and cliches live in anti_keywords.

fs-hover-only-purchase.text: Forbidden: the add-to-cart or quick-add control exists only while the pointer hovers the card. Touch users have no hover, and keyboard users may never trigger it. Instead keep the purchase control visible at rest, or reveal it on keyboard focus and on tap as well as on hover. Hover may add detail, never the only route to purchase.

fs-focus-indicator-removed.text: Forbidden: outline: none, or a focus style that blends into the card or background, on the card links, the add-to-cart button or the stepper. Instead keep a visible keyboard focus indicator with a perimeter of at least 2 CSS pixels and 3:1 contrast against the unfocused state (WCAG 2.2 Focus Appearance, 2.4.13).

fs-color-only-state.text: Forbidden: the added, out-of-stock or error state shown only by a change of color on the button or card. Instead pair the color with text in the control label or status message, and with an icon or a shape where an error needs to stand out, so the state survives color blindness and forced colors.
